note: Conversion batch #4: pairs the 12 functions newly implemented in src/postfit_tables.jl (core070 final-surface-slice-notes.md, one commit each: deviance, profile_cross_rho_ci, predict_cross_covariance, predict_missing, simulate_unit_trait, profile_cross_rho, rotate_loadings, extract_rotated_loadings_table, extract_coevolution_modules, imputed, tidy, summary) against their BLOCKED_NEEDS_JULIA_SURFACE ledger rows in docs/dev-log/core070/required-source-case-map.json (source_id prefix postfit/POSTFIT-SURFACE-*, excluding postfit/POSTFIT-SURFACE-impute_model, which is a DIFFERENT function not implemented in this slice, and postfit/POSTFIT-SURFACE-tidy, the bare-generic re-export row already BLOCKED_SPEC_DEFECT/compatibility_adapter-proposed, distinct from tidy.gllvmTMB_multi). 12 target rows total. 7 are executable on the reused gaussian_small fixture (deviance, tidy.gllvmTMB_multi, summary.gllvmTMB_multi, rotate_loadings, extract_rotated_loadings_table, predict_missing, simulate_unit_trait); 5 are deferred (extract_coevolution_modules, imputed.gllvmTMB, predict_cross_covariance, profile_cross_rho, profile_cross_rho_ci) because their R counterparts genuinely need a cross-lineage coevolution kernel fit or an mi()-predictor fit, and no such fixture is proven in this worktree's receipts (test/parity/ and .unlazy/core070-aghq/ contain no executed cross-lineage or mi() paired R+Julia fit) -- the same 'do not invent an unproven fixture in a lean batch' discipline wave-7 established for its phylo-fixture-absent rows. Design discipline: every R-side signature/return shape below was read directly from .unlazy/core070-aghq/oracle-source/readback/R/methods-gllvmTMB.R, rotate-loadings.R, and simulate-unit-trait.R -- never inferred from a Julia docstring. gaussian_small is reused VERBATIM from tools/core070_surface_conversion_batch.R / tools/core070_wave6_conversion_batch.R / tools/core070_wave7_conversion_batch.R (seed 42, p=5, K=2, n=80) -- the R formula ('value ~ 0 + trait + latent(...)') is UNCHANGED; the one addition on the JULIA side is that this batch's Julia child fits WITH an explicit X = one-hot trait design (p x n x p) so its beta coefficients are genuinely comparable to R's per-trait b_fix intercepts (deviance/predict_missing/rotate_loadings/extract_rotated_loadings_table do not depend on this addition and would be identical either way; tidy/summary's fixed-effect quantities need it to be a non-vacuous comparison -- R's fit has always had 5 non-trivial b_fix rows via its formula, wave-7 simply never exercised a Julia-side quantity that needed the matching X). Per the task brief: point/paired-fit cases use 1e-4; the summary/tidy fixed-effect and rotate_loadings tcrossprod-invariant cases use the same 1e-4 tier (point estimates, not SE/CI quantities, so no 5e-3 widening is needed here); predict_missing and simulate_unit_trait are STRUCTURAL-only (shape/finiteness/own-consistency, never a cross-engine numeric equality of a random draw or a masked-cell reconstruction that needs missing data neither fixture has).

gaussian_small.description: Reused VERBATIM from tools/core070_surface_conversion_batch.R / tools/core070_wave6_conversion_batch.R / tools/core070_wave7_conversion_batch.R (seed 42, p=5, K=2, n=80). R: value ~ 0 + trait + latent(0 + trait | site, d = 2, unique = FALSE), gaussian(), control = gllvmTMBcontrol(n_init = 1L, se = TRUE). Julia (this batch's addition): fit_gaussian_gllvm(Y_g; K=2, X=X_g) where X_g is the p x n x p one-hot trait design matching R's '0 + trait' dummy coding column-for-column (predictor t is 1 on trait row t, 0 elsewhere) -- so Julia's fitted beta is the same quantity as R's b_fix per-trait intercept, not a Julia-only zero-mean simplification.

simulate_unit_trait_params.description: Standalone (no fit dependency) DGP parameters shared by both languages for the structural simulate_unit_trait case: n_units=20, n_obs_per_unit=3, n_traits=4, Lambda_B (4x2), Lambda_W (4x1), psi_B=psi_W=rep(0.3,4), sigma2_eps=0.4. Each language draws with its OWN RNG (R seed=1 via set.seed(1); Julia StableRNG(1)) -- the parameter VALUES are shared for a symmetric read, but the case never compares the resulting random draws numerically across languages (task brief: simulate_unit_trait is RNG-independent, structural-only).

cases.notes: Verified from methods-gllvmTMB.R:2862-2864: deviance.gllvmTMB_multi(object, ...) is exactly -2*as.numeric(logLik(object, ...)), no null/saturated-model term. Julia: StatsAPI.deviance(fit::AnyGllvmFit) = -2*StatsAPI.loglikelihood(fit) (src/postfit_tables.jl:21), the identical algebraic definition -- deviance == -2*logLik holds EXACTLY (to floating-point) on EACH side by construction (mechanically, not merely asserted), so the cross-engine comparison here IS the cross-engine logLik-delta comparison the task brief asks for, doubled: |deviance_r - deviance_j| = 2*|logLik_r - logLik_j|. Tolerance 1e-3 (roughly double wave6/wave7's 1e-4 point-quantity tier, since deviance is -2x logLik and this is the first case pairing a DOUBLED quantity) rather than re-deriving a separate identity-check case -- the algebraic identity itself needs no live-run verification, it is true of both functions' source code unconditionally.

cases.julia_call: [r.estimate for r in GLLVM.tidy(fit_j, Y_g; X = X_g)]
cases.notes: Verified from methods-gllvmTMB.R:1177-1215: tidy.gllvmTMB_multi(x, effects='fixed') (the default) returns data.frame(term, estimate, std.error, ...) from .gllvmTMB_b_fix_table(x) -- 5 rows (trait1..trait5 intercepts) in trait-level order (t1..t5), matching gaussian_small's df_g trait factor level order. Julia: tidy(fit::GllvmFit, Y; effects=(:fixed,)) (src/postfit_tables.jl:898, default) calls coef_table(fit, Y; parm='beta', X) and returns one NamedTuple per fixed coefficient in the SAME column order as X_g's third dimension, which this batch constructs as a one-hot trait design (predictor t = 1 on trait row t) column-for-column matching R's '0 + trait' dummy coding -- so row i on both sides is the estimate for trait i's intercept. Y_g row-demeaning in the fixture DGP (Y_g <- Y_g - rowMeans(Y_g)) means both sides' estimates are expected to be small (near zero, not exactly zero: the fitted per-trait intercept absorbs residual sample mean after the latent-variable component is fit jointly, not a separate two-stage demeaning), which is why the paired-fit 1e-4 point tier (not a looser SE tier) is used -- this is a POINT ESTIMATE comparison, not a standard-error comparison.

cases.julia_call: s = summary(fit_j, Y_g; X = X_g); vcat([r.estimate for r in s.fixef], s.logLik)
cases.notes: Verified from methods-gllvmTMB.R:744-863: summary.gllvmTMB_multi(object)$fixef is .gllvmTMB_b_fix_table(object) (identical underlying table/order to tidy(effects='fixed') above -- same 5-row per-trait-intercept comparison, exercised through the SEPARATE summary() code path rather than tidy()'s, per the distinct ledger row) and $header$logLik is -object$opt$objective (the maximised log-likelihood, unpenalised/non-mspl/non-weighted path, which gaussian_small is). Julia: Base.summary(fit::GllvmFit, Y; X) (src/postfit_tables.jl:1011) returns a GllvmSummary with fixef = tidy(...)[:fixed tier] and logLik = fit.logLik. Combined into one 6-element point vector (5 fixef estimates + 1 logLik) rather than two cases, since both quantities are read off the SAME summary() call and this ledger row (summary.gllvmTMB_multi) is paid once, not twice; Sigma_B/Sigma_W/ICC/communality/se_status are NOT compared here -- Sigma_B/Sigma_W/ICC/communality already have their own separate required-source-case-map rows (extract_Sigma / extract_ICC_site / extract_communality) covered elsewhere in the ledger, and se_status is a categorical diagnostic classification, not a point quantity.

cases.julia_call: rot = GLLVM.rotate_loadings(fit_j, Y_g; level = :unit, method = :varimax); vec(rot.Lambda * rot.Lambda')
cases.notes: Verified from rotate-loadings.R:90-217 ('The rotation is applied ... so implied covariance Lambda Lambda^T is unchanged' for the orthogonal varimax T) and src/postfit_tables.jl:513-579 (same varimax-orthogonal-T convention). Ground rule (this repo's general convention, also used by wave7's own_consistency case): never compare SIGNED Lambda entries directly across two independently-fit/independently-rotated models -- rotation and sign are not identifiable, so raw rot$Lambda vs rot.Lambda would be comparing two different arbitrary bases. tcrossprod(Lambda_rotated) = Lambda_rotated %*% t(Lambda_rotated) IS rotation-and-sign INVARIANT (unchanged by any orthogonal T, by construction) and equals the model-implied Sigma_B-loadings-block ΛΛᵀ on each side -- a genuinely IDENTIFIABLE, paired-fit-comparable p x p quantity (flattened to a 25-element vector, column-major on both sides via R's as.numeric(matrix) and Julia's vec(), the same convention this ledger's other cases use).

Verified from rotate-loadings.R:282-378: extract_rotated_loadings_table(fit, level='unit', method='varimax' default) returns one row per (trait, axis) -- nrow = length(trait_names)*length(axis_names) = p*d = 5*2 = 10 on gaussian_small -- with axis_share = axis_variance/sum(axis_variance), REPEATED once per trait within each axis (rep(axis_share, each=length(trait_names)), :328), so summing the UNIQUE per-axis axis_share values (not the raw column, which double-counts by p) must equal 1.0 to float precision whenever axis_total>0 (:325-329). Julia: extract_rotated_loadings_table (src/postfit_tables.jl:608-661) builds the identical axis-major row layout (nrow = p*d) with the identical axis_share = axis_variance/total_axis_var construction (:637,652). This is a STRUCTURAL/own-consistency verdict (nrow==p*d AND the per-axis axis_share values sum to 1 on EACH side independently) rather than a cross-engine numeric pairing of table cells -- the underlying identifiable quantity (trace(Lambda Lambda^T), which axis_variance sums to) is already paired cross-engine by CORE070-WAVE8-ROTATE-LOADINGS-LLT-INVARIANT above; re-pairing it here through the table's row/column packaging would test the SAME number twice under two different names, not a distinct fact.

Verified from methods-gllvmTMB.R:3948-4085 docstring's explicit @return note: 'A complete-data fit (no masked cells) returns a zero-row data frame with the same columns.' gaussian_small has no missing()/miss_control(response='include') declaration, so R's predict_missing(fit_g) returns 0 rows. Julia's predict_missing(fit, Y; mask=nothing) docstring (src/postfit_tables.jl:190-217) states the identical equivalence explicitly: 'mask = nothing (default) means every cell is observed, giving a zero-row result (R's complete-data behaviour)'. This is the ONE predict_missing case buildable WITHOUT inventing a new missing-response fixture (which neither language's reused fixtures carry) -- it tests the documented complete-data degenerate case on both sides, not the masked-cell reconstruction machinery itself (which needs a genuine missing-data fit and is out of this lean batch's scope, same class of gap as wave7's deferred phylo/mi rows).

cases.r_call: sim <- simulate_unit_trait(n_units = 20, n_obs_per_unit = 3, n_traits = 4, Lambda_B = <4x2>, Lambda_W = <4x1>, psi_B = rep(0.3,4), psi_W = rep(0.3,4), sigma2_eps = 0.4, seed = 1)
cases.julia_call: GLLVM.simulate_unit_trait(StableRNG(1); n_units = 20, n_obs_per_unit = 3, n_traits = 4, K_B = 2, K_W = 1, Lambda_B = <4x2>, Lambda_W = <4x1>, psi_B = fill(0.3,4), psi_W = fill(0.3,4), sigma2_eps = 0.4)
cases.notes: Per the task brief: simulate_unit_trait is RNG-independent -- the two languages' random draws are never compared numerically, only STRUCTURE (shapes, ranges, finiteness), matching how imputed() is also scoped structural-only. Verified from simulate-unit-trait.R:78-164: R's sim$data is a LONG data.frame with one row per (unit, observation, trait), so nrow(sim$data) = n_units*n_obs_per_unit*n_traits = 20*3*4 = 240; sim$truth$Lambda_B is n_traits x d_B = 4x2. Julia's simulate_unit_trait (src/postfit_tables.jl:275-321) returns a WIDE Y matrix n_traits x (n_units*n_obs_per_unit) = 4x60 (240 elements total, matching R's row count element-for-element as the one legitimate cross-engine structural invariant -- both DGPs draw the SAME total number of (unit,obs,trait) scalar observations from the SAME n_units/n_obs_per_unit/n_traits arguments, a fact of the shared argument contract, not of either RNG stream) and truth.Lambda_B is n_traits x K_B = 4x2, matching R's Lambda_B shape used as input on both sides. Both sides independently assert all(is.finite(...)) on their own simulated values (no non-finite y from a well-posed positive-definite Sigma_B/Sigma_W) and the Lambda_B shape read back from truth equals what was supplied.

deferred.reason: src/postfit_tables.jl:719-767's own scope note restricts this slice to scale=:shape, operating directly on a caller-supplied Sigma_shared matrix from a genuine cross-lineage coevolution fit (e.g. fit_coevolution_gaussian's Lambda*Lambda', or extract_Sigma(part=:shared) on a phylo-loadings coevolution fit). No such fixture is reused by this batch's proven recipes (gaussian_small / simulate_unit_trait_params); building and validating a coevolution/cross-kernel fixture pair (R+Julia) on both a live gllvmTMB kernel_*() formula fit and a matching GLLVM.jl fit_coevolution_gaussian call is a genuine new-fixture slice, out of this lean batch's reuse-only scope -- same class of gap as wave7's deferred extract_Gamma row (wave7-conversion-batch-contract.json's deferred[], which named the identical Sigma_phy/cross-kernel fixture absence).

Verified from missing-predictor.R:2597-2725: imputed.gllvmTMB(object, variable, rows, se) requires object$missing_data$predictors to be a non-empty list -- i.e. a genuine R gllvmTMB() fit using an mi() missing-predictor formula term, and aborts loudly otherwise ('This fit has no modelled missing predictors to summarize'). gaussian_small has no mi() term. Julia's imputed(fitmi, x) (src/postfit_tables.jl:801-812) instead requires a fit_gaussian_mi_fiml(...) result (a NamedTuple carrying an eblup_x field) -- a DIFFERENT Gaussian-FIML machinery, not necessarily the same estimator/model class as R's mi() formula route (R's own docstring documents its estimates as 'conditional modes, not conditional means, multiple-imputation draws, or posterior summaries' from a specific joint-likelihood augmentation; the Julia FIML route's own docstring does not claim byte-for-byte equivalence to that route). Building an R mi()-formula fixture, verifying its exact estimator equivalence to fit_gaussian_mi_fiml, and pairing the two is a genuine new-fixture + estimator-equivalence design slice, out of this lean batch's scope; the task brief's own 'imputed: RNG-independent structural checks' framing (paired with simulate_unit_trait) presupposes a fixture that does not yet exist in this worktree's receipts for the imputed()-specific case (as opposed to predict_missing's zero-row complete-data degenerate case, which needed no such fixture and is executable above).

src/postfit_tables.jl:116-140's own contract requires a genuine n x n cross-lineage kernel K (e.g. from make_cross_kernel) and extract_Gamma's Lambda_phy-bearing fit -- the identical cross-lineage/coevolution fixture gap as extract_coevolution_modules above and wave7's deferred extract_Gamma row. No such fixture is proven in this worktree's receipts; deferred rather than invented under this batch's lean scope.

src/postfit_tables.jl:337-369's own contract requires a caller-supplied refit(K, rho) callable targeting e.g. fit_coevolution_gaussian/fit_coevolution_blockna, over the SAME cross-lineage kernel machinery (make_cross_kernel(A_H, A_P, W; rho)) as predict_cross_covariance/extract_coevolution_modules above -- no A_H/A_P/W cross-lineage fixture (host tree, parasite tree, association matrix) is proven in this worktree's receipts, and R's profile_cross_rho() (kernel-helpers.R:166-262) needs a matching live gllvmTMB kernel_*() coevolution formula fit to refit against. Same fixture-absence class as the two rows above; deferred.

profile_cross_rho_ci(rho, delta_deviance; level) (src/postfit_tables.jl:61-109) is pure grid-interpolation post-processing over a (rho, delta_deviance) TABLE -- it does not itself need a live fit -- but the only defensible way to generate a genuinely R-vs-Julia-comparable (rho, delta_deviance) table is to run profile_cross_rho on both sides first (the deferred row immediately above), since fabricating a synthetic delta_deviance grid by hand would not exercise anything about either engine's real coevolution-kernel machinery and would risk a vacuous pass. Deferred alongside profile_cross_rho for the same cross-lineage fixture absence; a follow-up wave that first lands the cross-lineage fixture pair can then chain profile_cross_rho's own table straight into this case.

rejection_cases.expect: Both engines refuse an unrecognised `level` value -- a genuine matching-refusal case (not an asymmetry): R's match.arg(level, c('unit','unit_obs','B','W')) errors on an unlisted value (rotate-loadings.R:96); Julia's rotate_loadings requires level === :unit and throws ArgumentError otherwise (src/postfit_tables.jl:517-519, this slice's GllvmFit-only scope reduction covers only :unit, so any other symbol -- including a genuinely bogus one -- is refused the same way).
rejection_cases.notes: Unlike wave7's REJ-CHECK-AUTO-RESIDUAL-NOT-A-FIT (a documented ASYMMETRY, R refuses a type Julia's check_auto_residual does not type-guard), this rejection case is SYMMETRIC: both engines validate the `level` argument and both refuse an unrecognised value. Included per the task brief's per-side expectation-fields discipline even where both sides agree, to keep the verifier's rejection-case machinery exercised by this batch rather than only copy-pasted from wave7's asymmetric example.
